pages.text: A $(item)regular engine$() delivers nothing until you right-click one of its end blocks with a $(item)Shaft$(). The shaft sticks out of the free end; a wrench takes it back off. You can put one at each end, the power is then split between the two.

The $(item)radial engine$() has its outputs built in: at both ends of a row, and on both sides of a single block. The $(item)turbine engine$() also has a built-in output, at one end only: look for the shaft stub on its model. Neither needs a shaft item.

Engine blocks join when they are the same block, face the same way and, for regular engines, have the same type. A row holds up to $(item)5 blocks$() by default (config $(item)engineMaxLength$()). Torque grows with every block in the row.
The 3D view shows a three-block I engine facing north, its shaft in front. Pipe fuel into any block: the row shares one fuel tank of 4000 mB.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
